R1.description: The end of a worker turn alone never makes a worker or job terminal while owned asynchronous work remains (AC1)

R2.description: Background Bash tasks keep the job non-terminal (AC2)

R3.description: Monitor tasks keep the job non-terminal (AC3)

R4.description: Scheduled wakeups keep the job non-terminal; a wakeup fire is recognised only by its measured, correlated command_lifecycle bracket, and a wakeup that is never delivered fails closed (AC4)

R5.description: Descendant processes launched by the worker, including ones that left its process group or were reparented, stay owned by the job until they finish or are explicitly abandoned (AC5)

R6.description: The lifecycle lock cannot be released while owned action work is still active, including across Controller loss (AC6)

R7.description: A later checkpoint or action cannot start while prior owned work is still active (AC7)

R8.description: Same-phase durable progress is recognised by one shared rule, e.g. IMPLEMENTING -> IMPLEMENTING with last_completed_checkpoint_id advancing and committed (AC8)

R9.description: Existing fail-closed recovery semantics remain intact for genuinely ambiguous or failed attempts (AC9)

R10.description: Controller interruption or restart recovers a waiting or draining job without duplicating the worker or losing ownership of the pending action (AC10)

R11.description: follow, inspect, status and explain distinguish an active worker, a waiting worker, background-owned work, an ended worker and pending reconciliation (AC11)

R12.description: Regression tests for the observed IMPLEMENTING, SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION and APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK failures, built from their real stream shapes (AC12)

R13.description: Regression: checkpoint N+1 cannot start while checkpoint N still owns background verification (AC13)

R14.description: Regression: a waiting worker resumes after its background task or wakeup completes and then finishes normally (AC14)

R15.description: Regression: a Controller restart during the waiting state neither duplicates the worker nor loses the pending action (AC15)

R16.description: The harness contract the fix relies on is measured, pinned by fixtures and an opt-in live probe, and every limitation that needs the future Harness Adapter Protocol is documented

R17.description: Developed and proven against the installed Workflow 2.5.1 with no Workflow edits; operator documentation and full verification

R18.description: The wakeup-fire recogniser is grounded in the captured harness fixtures: result origin is never evidence; a command_lifecycle started/completed pair is correlated by command_uuid around exactly one turn; missing, duplicated, reordered, delayed, overlapping, malformed or unmatched lifecycle events and stalled brackets fail closed, survive Controller restart by replay, and are exposed by the diagnostics; a matched wakeup stays owned work until a stop whose harness-reported count agrees, or a settle window sized by the overdue lateness bound, settles it, so an unrelated bracket cannot end the session before the real fire (amendment 0, round 9)
